newsitem.title: BULGARIA: Bulgaria lev firms on c.bank support, profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Bulgaria lev firms on c.bank support, profit-taking.

text.p: The Bulgarian lev rose to around 1,630-1,650 per dollar at the close from 1,670-1,680 at midday due to central bank support and a subsequent rise in foreign currency supply for profit taking, dealers said.
"(Foreign currency) supply from banks and clients rose on profit taking after the central bank halted the lev fall around midday. Dollar demand was subdued in the afternoon," a bank dealer said.

The lev fell to 1,750-1,950 per dollar in early trade on Monday from Friday's close at about 1,685-1,700 on a nervous and a dollar bullish interbank market following a cut in the central bank main interest rate, dealers said.
Dollar sales by the central bank at 1,700-1,710 levs stabilised the lev and reversed the fall.
A recommendation by the interim cabinet on Monday to peg the lev to the mark as an anchor currency under a fixed exchange rate mechanism has not triggered a rush on the mark, traders said.
The central bank cut its main interest rate to 4.29 percent monthly from 5.20 percent, effective from Monday.
Central bank governor Lybomir Filipov told reporters on Monday now the bank was strong enough to support the lev near its current levels.
Interim prime minister Stefan Sofianski told reporters on Monday central bank foreign exchange reserves have risen to $1.25 billion at mid-May from $1.146 billion at end-April.
